summary.title: JavaScript template engine in just 20 lines
summary.one_liner: You learn how a tiny JavaScript template engine works by building one step by step, using regular expressions, a cursor, and the new Function constructor to compile templates into functions.
keywords: template with loops and if statements
takeaways: Placeholders like <%expr%> can be found with a global regular expression and exec in a while loop.
Template text and JavaScript can be compiled into a function body that pushes strings into an array and joins them.
new Function(code).apply(data) runs the generated function with data as this, so this.name resolves to data.name.
Lines starting with keywords such as if, for, else or braces must be inserted as raw JavaScript rather than pushed, which enables loops and conditionals in templates.
summary.summary: The author, building the AbsurdJS preprocessor, explains a small pure-JavaScript template engine adapted from John Resig's idea. The article builds the engine incrementally: it finds <% %> blocks with a regex, replaces them naively, then switches to compiling the template into a generated function body using new Function. It handles quoting issues, nested properties via this, and control flow such as for and if/else by detecting keyword lines. The final version is about 15 lines.
